definition: CuPy is a NumPy-compatible array library that runs on NVIDIA (and AMD) GPUs.
details: Created by Preferred Networks for the Chainer framework in 2015; now an independent open-source project.

explainer.lead: How to install CuPy, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import cupy as cp

x = cp.random.rand(4096, 4096, dtype=cp.float32)
y = x @ x.T                 # runs on the GPU
print(float(y.mean()))
host = cp.asnumpy(y)        # copy back to NumPy

explainer.inAi: Move heavy array maths (similarity matrices, preprocessing) onto the GPU with almost no code changes.
explainer.jsNote: CuPy is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It's the same set of tools you already use for number crunching, but it runs on a graphics card so it goes much faster.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers swap numpy.* for cupy.* to accelerate multi-dimensional arrays, sparse matrices and linear algebra, and can write custom GPU kernels. A pitfall is that code must actually suit GPU execution to benefit from the drop-in swap.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source library for GPU-accelerated computing in Python providing NumPy/SciPy-compatible APIs for multi-dimensional arrays, sparse matrices and numerical algorithms, supporting NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm (from v9.0). Limits follow from GPU platform and memory constraints.

explainer.example: A team replaces numpy calls with cupy calls on a CUDA GPU to run the same array and linear algebra code on accelerated hardware.
